# Jacksonville Jaguars at San Diego Chargers

**Regular-season Week 4**  
Sunday, September 28, 2014 | 4:05 p.m. ET | Qualcomm Stadium, San Diego, California  
**Final: San Diego Chargers 21, Jacksonville Jaguars 20**

## 1. Preparation and final game-day decisions

Stone's plan of September 21 governed the week, and it changed one operation: from this game Stone called the defense, with Romeo Crennel staying the coordinator, running the defensive meetings and sending each call in to Daryl Smith. The backfield was set as an order rather than a committee, Maurice Jones-Drew first, C.J. Anderson second and Jonathan Grimes third, and the tight ends were given more designed work without a target count. Monday, September 22, was the Indianapolis review and the San Diego introduction, with eight defensive calls walked from Stone to Crennel to Smith at walkthrough pace. Wednesday was the base, tight-end, Quarters and Cover 6 practice, Thursday the Dime and Replace installation and the special plays, Friday the scoring, four-minute, two-minute and kicking periods, and Saturday the hotel and stadium review in San Diego.

**Plan in force:** Stone's defensive calls through Crennel, and Jones-Drew's normal-down role ahead of Anderson by called series ([the September 21 plan](Week%204%20Packet_%20at%20San%20Diego.md)).  
**Game-day availability:** Travis Kelce was cleared and Aqib Talib's independent hold was released on September 25, and Davante Adams was cleared on September 26 after missing the week's practices; all three played. Malcolm Butler and Jordan Poyer stayed out under their independent holds. The seven inactives were applied as Stone set them on September 27, and Hakeem Nicks dressed for the first time this season without taking a snap.

## 2. Pregame media

**Reporter:** Can you go through the injury report?

**Stone:** Malcolm and Jordan are out. Both are in the independent process and neither one practiced this week. Aqib was released Thursday, the date he was given, and he practiced Thursday and today. Travis was cleared Thursday and practiced both days. Davante was cleared today. He didn't practice, and he's questionable.

**Reporter:** Are you going to call the defensive plays on Sunday?

**Stone:** I am. I call it, Romeo sends it in to Daryl, and Daryl gets it to the huddle with the strength and the motion check. Romeo is still the coordinator. He ran the defensive meetings this week and he gives Daryl what he needs between snaps. We walked the relay Monday, eight times through. Mike stays beside me with the offensive sheet and Charlie has the clock. The first three games were Romeo's calls.

## 3. The game

San Diego won by a point because Jacksonville turned its first two chances into three points and ran out of downs on its last one. Josh Scobee missed from 47 at the end of the opening drive, the defense's only takeaway produced a field goal, and after Andrew Hawkins's touchdown with 2:53 left made it 21-20, the offense got the ball back at its own 6 with 1:39 to play and no timeouts.

### First quarter

The opening drive went eleven plays from the Jacksonville 10 to the San Diego 29, where Scobee's 47-yard try on fourth-and-4 missed. Three plays later A.J. Bouye came off the slot on third-and-11, stripped Philip Rivers and recovered the ball at the San Diego 29. Jacksonville gained 7 and Scobee kicked a 40-yarder at 5:39.

### Second quarter

San Diego answered with a twelve-play, 80-yard drive kept alive by Danny Woodhead's 26-yard run on fourth-and-6; he scored from 19 on second-and-16 at 13:04. Jacksonville went 80 yards in eight plays, Adams catching 29 on the Bunch Mesh and Jones-Drew taking the Snag throw in from the 1 at 8:49. Rivers found Antonio Gates for a 12-yard touchdown at 4:41, and the half ended with San Diego at the Jacksonville 34, ahead 14-10.

### Third quarter

San Diego punted twice and Jacksonville once before Jacksonville drove from its 13 to the San Diego 15, where Corey Liuget's sack stopped the drive's progress, and Scobee's 36-yard field goal at 3:25 made it 14-13. San Diego then held the ball for 6:41.

### Fourth quarter

That drive went fourteen plays and 75 yards and ended with Keenan Allen's 1-yard touchdown catch at 11:44. Jacksonville's next possession lost 13 yards, but from its 12 the offense went fourteen plays: Jones-Drew converted fourth-and-2 at the San Diego 34 for 3 on Counter Right, and Cousins hit Hawkins for 7 on the Boot Flood Right at 2:53, Scobee's kick making it 21-20. Jacksonville spent two timeouts on San Diego's next possession and got the punt back, fair-caught at its 6 with 1:39 left and none remaining. Adam Thielen caught 33 on third-and-3, and from the Jacksonville 46 four throws fell incomplete, the last on fourth-and-10 with 35 seconds left.

### The calls and decisions that shaped the game

The first decision was the kick on the opening drive: no score, fourth-and-4 at the San Diego 29, and Stone sent Scobee out for a 47-yarder that missed. The play-by-play records the call and the result and nothing about the snap, the hold or the protection; Stone said afterwards that all three would be gone through before anyone put it on the kick. The last sequence turned on the clock: two Jacksonville timeouts went on San Diego's final possession, so the offense started at its own 6 with 1:39 left and nothing to stop the clock with. The game book records the four incompletions from the 46; it does not record the coverage on them, and nothing here explains why each one fell.

## 4. Postgame media

**Stone:** One point. We kicked from 47 on the first drive and missed, we got three out of the takeaway, and we started the last drive at our 6 with no timeouts left. The decisions in there are mine. Go ahead.

**Reporter:** What did you make of the sequence at the end? Near the end there where you used your timeouts --

**Stone:** We spent two on their last possession and got the ball at our 6 with 1:39 and none left. I'll look at how those were spent.

**Reporter:** On fourth-and-4 at their 29 on the first drive, did you think maybe of going for it?

**Stone:** No score, first drive, fourth-and-4 at their 29. I kicked it and Josh missed from 47. Mike goes through the snap, the hold and the protection with him before anybody puts it on the kick.

## 5. Football review and next week's work

**Offense:** Cousins played the season's first game without a turnover, and the offense finished two long drives, the 80 yards before the half and the fourteen plays to the late touchdown. It did not finish the first two trips: a missed kick and a short field after the takeaway turned into three points.  
**Defense:** Bouye's strip sack was the one takeaway, and two San Diego touchdown drives of twelve and fourteen plays decided the margin. Woodhead's 26-yard run on fourth-and-6 kept the first of them going.  
**Special teams and game management:** The opening miss and the timeout use on San Diego's last possession are the two decisions the staff carried into the Pittsburgh week.  
**What changes for the next game:** Stone said the snap, the hold and the protection on the 47-yard miss would be gone through, and that he would look at how the late timeouts were spent. Both are reviews still to be held, not changes made.

## 6. After-action report

### Injuries and availability changes

No one was removed from the game. Julian Stanford (lower extremity, minor) was limited with no projected time lost; Paul Posluszny (trunk, minor) was out with a projected return of October 3; Adrian Phillips (lower extremity, minor) was out with a projected return of September 29. Each had a reassessment set for September 29. Butler's and Poyer's holds were unchanged.

### Players who stood out

A.J. Bouye forced and recovered the only turnover. Davante Adams caught 8 passes for 98 yards, the 29-yard catch on the touchdown drive among them. For San Diego, Woodhead's fourth-and-6 run started the first touchdown drive.

### Role or transaction consequences

No changes.

## 7. Final record and next game

**Record after game:** 3-1.  
**Standing / playoff result:** First in the AFC South at 3-1, tied with Houston and ahead of it on division record.  
**Next scheduled event:** Week 5 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday, October 5, 1 p.m. ET, EverBank Field.
